# PSSA3.SA Technical Analysis Report
**Analysis date:** 2026-09-14 | **Benchmark:** ^BVSP | **Horizon:** ~20 trading days after the first close following the analysis date

## 1. Verified snapshot (source of truth)
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Open / High / Low / Close | 49.4687 / 49.7456 / 48.5685 / 49.4983 |
| Volume | 996,100 |
| close_10_ema | 49.8286 |
| close_50_sma | 50.8812 |
| close_200_sma | 48.7155 |
| RSI | 49.0429 |
| Bollinger middle / upper / lower | 48.6106 / 52.0662 / 45.1550 |
| MACD / signal / histogram | 0.0957 / -0.2247 / 0.3203 |
| ATR | 1.2454 |

No discrepancies were found between the verified snapshot and the indicator series returned by the other tools for 2026-09-14 (RSI 49.04, 50-SMA 50.88, 200-SMA 48.72, MACD histogram 0.3203, ATR 1.2454 all match).

## 2. Price trend
- **Longer arc:** The stock rose from roughly 46–47 in September 2025 to a peak close of 54.8498 on 2026-07-22 (intraday high 54.9487) and 54.6223 on 2026-07-15/16. It then sold off.
- **Pullback:** Between 2026-08-06 (52.0801) and 2026-08-14 (46.0758), the close fell about 12%. The sell-off was steepest on 2026-08-07 (close 49.8742, volume 3.88M, roughly 2x the typical daily volume), which points to a high-volume distribution day.
- **Recovery:** From the 2026-08-19 low close (45.9967) the stock rebounded to 51.1008 on 2026-09-04. Closes then eased to 49.4983 on 2026-09-14.
- **Current position:** Price sits about 2.7% below the 50-SMA (50.88) and about 1.6% above the 200-SMA (48.72). It is also below the 10-EMA (49.83).

## 3. Indicator read
- **Moving averages:** The 50-SMA is flat-to-declining (51.76 on 2026-08-17 down to 50.88 on 2026-09-14), so medium-term trend has turned neutral to weak. The 200-SMA is rising very slowly (48.34 to 48.72 over the same window), which keeps the long-term bias mildly positive. Price is trading between the two. The 10-EMA is below price's recent highs and acting as near-term resistance.
- **MACD histogram:** Turned negative on 2026-08-19 (-0.6372 trough area around -0.82 on 08-17) and turned positive on 2026-08-26. It peaked at 0.6207 on 2026-09-04 and has since shrunk to 0.3203. Momentum is still positive but fading for five sessions. The MACD line (0.0957) is just above the signal line (-0.2247).
- **RSI:** Recovered from oversold territory (28.9 on 2026-08-19) to 60.9 on 2026-09-04, then fell back to 49.04. This is a neutral reading with no extreme on either side. The pattern shows a sharp swing from oversold to moderately overbought within about two weeks.
- **Bollinger Bands:** Middle band 48.61, upper 52.07, lower 45.16. Price sits in the upper-middle part of the band, with room toward the upper band before a stretched reading. The band width (~6.9 points) is consistent with ATR of 1.25.
- **VWMA:** 49.65 is slightly above the close (49.50). VWMA was below the price for most of late August and crossed back above it in early September, which supports the rebound. The recent slight dip in price has not yet pushed VWMA under the close.
- **ATR:** 1.25 (~2.5% of price). This is a reasonable baseline for a 4-week stop distance, roughly 1.5–2 ATR (~1.9–2.5 points) below entry.

## 4. Key levels (from verified data only)
- **Resistance:** 50-SMA ~50.88; recent swing high ~51.11 (2026-09-04 close); upper Bollinger ~52.07.
- **Support:** 10-EMA ~49.83 (now acting as resistance); 200-SMA ~48.72; Bollinger middle ~48.61; recent swing low 46.08 (2026-08-14) and 45.997 (2026-08-19).

## 5. Outlook for the 20-trading-day horizon (relative to ^BVSP)
- **Bias:** Neutral, with a slight tilt toward the bullish side given the positive MACD histogram, VWMA above price, and price above the 200-SMA.
- **Bull case:** A close above the 50-SMA (~50.9) and a reclaim of the 51.1 swing high would target the upper Bollinger band (~52) and the late-July highs (~54.5–54.8).
- **Bear case:** A close below the 200-SMA (~48.7) would negate the recent recovery and open a retest of the August lows (~46.0).
- **Caveat:** This analysis covers only the stock's own technical data. I did not retrieve ^BVSP data, so relative performance versus the index is not assessed here. Fundamental drivers and news are also outside the scope of these tools.

# PSSA3.SA (Porto Seguro S.A.): Market Context Report, 2026-09-14

**Bottom line:** The news flow on PSSA3.SA this week is thin, with no material company event. The call over the next 20 trading days will depend mainly on Brazil's rate path and the macro backdrop, not on company news. My tools did not surface sector-specific or stock-price news, so treat the company read as incomplete.

## 1. Company-specific news (2026-09-07 to 2026-09-14)

- The only CVM filings in the window are two monthly reports of securities held by insiders and related parties, delivered 2026-09-10 (CVM art. 11). These are routine and carry no clear directional signal.
- No earnings release, guidance change, dividend announcement, M&A, or regulatory action appeared in the search. Porto Seguro's next quarterly results (2Q26) would already be out, so I could not verify them here.
- Gap: the news tool returns only CVM filing metadata, not article content, and Yahoo global news did not cover the window. Sentiment, analyst revisions, and price reaction are unverified.

## 2. Brazil macro backdrop (data from Banco Central do Brasil)

| Indicator | Latest | Trend / Context |
|---|---|---|
| Selic target (Copom) | 14.00% (2026-09-14) | Down from 14.75% at end-March; cuts of 25bp at a time |
| Focus Selic, end-2026 median | 13.75% (survey 2026-09-11) | Drifted down from 14.00% in late June, flat for 4 weeks |
| Focus Selic, end-2027 median | 12.00% | Market pricing a steady easing cycle |
| Focus Selic, end-2028 median | 10.50% | Implies a long, gradual path toward neutral |
| IPCA 12m | 4.22% (Aug 2026) | Peaked at 4.72% in May, falling for three months |
| USD/BRL PTAX | 5.1696 (2026-09-14) | Roughly flat since end-June (5.18 at end-Aug); BRL range-bound |

**Interpretation:** Disinflation is underway (IPCA 12m down from 4.72% to 4.22%) and the Selic has been cut about 75bp since March. The Focus survey expects further easing into 2027–28. For an insurer-type stock, falling rates tend to support valuations and reduce the discount rate applied to long-duration liabilities. They can also hurt financial-income yields on float. On balance, the rate path is mildly supportive.

## 3. Global and prediction-market context

- Global news for the window was not available from the tool, so I cannot assess external risk sentiment this week.
- Prediction-market odds for the Brazil election were withheld for today's date (the tool serves only live odds, not a 2026-09-14 snapshot). Brazil's October election is a real risk factor for the BRL, rates, and local equities, but I cannot quantify it from these tools.

## 4. Trading implications for the 4-week horizon (vs. ^BVSP)

- **Relative drivers:** Porto Seguro is a defensive, domestic-facing name. Its relative performance vs. the Ibovespa depends on (a) rate-cut expectations, which are supportive, and (b) election-related risk-off moves, which hit the index heavily and could favor defensives. Direction is unclear.
- **Lean:** Neutral to mildly positive on the macro rate backdrop, with no company catalyst identified. Confidence is low because company-specific data is missing.
- **What would change the view:** A Focus Selic revision upward (back toward 14%+) would signal a stalled easing cycle and weigh on the name. A sharp BRL depreciation would pressure rates and sentiment. Any 2Q26 results or guidance commentary not captured here should be checked before sizing a position.

## Summary table

| Item | Finding | Signal for PSSA3.SA (4-wk vs. ^BVSP) |
|---|---|---|
| Company filings (wk of 9/7–9/14) | Insider holdings reports only (9/10) | Neutral |
| Company news/earnings | Not found in tools | Unknown; verify |
| Selic | 14.00%, cut 75bp since March | Mildly positive |
| Focus Selic end-2026 / 2027 | 13.75% / 12.00%, stable | Mildly positive (easing priced in) |
| IPCA 12m | 4.22%, falling from 4.72% peak | Positive (disinflation) |
| USD/BRL | 5.17, range-bound | Neutral |
| Brazil election odds | Not available for today | Key unquantified risk |
| Global news | Not available | Unknown |

**Overall:** Neutral-to-slightly-positive, low conviction. Confirm company fundamentals and recent price action before taking a relative position.

Bull Analyst: # Bull Case for PSSA3.SA: Constructive Into a Reclaim of 50-SMA

Bear analyst, I expect you'll lead with the two things that look worst on the chart: the stock sits below its declining 50-day average, and the momentum histogram has shrunk for five straight sessions. I'll address both. But first, here is what the data shows.

## 1. The Long-Term Uptrend Hasn't Broken

PSSA3.SA climbed from roughly 46–47 in September 2025 to a peak close of 54.85 on July 22, 2026. The August sell-off took it to 46.08, about 12% lower. Since the August 19 low of 46.00, the stock has recovered to 51.10 and currently trades at 49.50.

The 200-day SMA sits at 48.72 and is still rising, so the long-term structure remains intact. The stock is about 1.6% above that line. Any bearish case has to explain why a stock in a 12-month uptrend should lose its long-term support after one pullback. I don't think the data supports that.

## 2. The Sell-Off Looks Like a Washout, Not a Breakdown

RSI fell to 28.9 on August 19, a clearly oversold reading, and the stock bounced sharply from there. By September 4 RSI had recovered to 60.9. That is a textbook momentum reset: heavy selling exhausted itself at a higher low than the July peak and was followed by a recovery that the bears haven't been able to reverse.

Yes, August 7 showed about 3.9 million shares traded, roughly twice normal volume, on a down day. I'd rather read that as a flush that cleared weak hands than as proof of ongoing distribution. The stock has since held above the 200-day average through the most recent decline.

## 3. Momentum Is Cooling, Not Turning

Concede the fact: the MACD histogram peaked at 0.62 on September 4 and is now 0.32. But the MACD line (0.096) is still above its signal line (-0.225), and the histogram remains positive. That is a deceleration within an uptrend. A real bearish turn would show a bearish crossover, and that hasn't happened.

VWMA at 49.65 sits just above the close. That is a mild caution flag, and I won't dismiss it. But it means the volume-weighted average price is close to where the stock is trading, not that sellers have taken control.

## 4. The Macro Backdrop Favors a Domestic Insurer

This is where the bear's case is weakest. The Selic has been cut 75 basis points since March, to 14.00%. Focus survey expectations point to 13.75% at end-2026, 12.00% at end-2027, and 10.50% at end-2028. IPCA 12-month inflation has fallen from 4.72% in May to 4.22% in August.

For an insurer like Porto Seguro, a falling discount rate supports the valuation of long-duration liabilities, and an easing cycle is generally supportive for domestic, defensive names. Falling rates can compress financial-income yields on float, and I'll grant that. But the market already prices a multi-year easing path, so a stall, not a cut, would be the surprise.

## 5. The Election Risk Is Real, but Symmetric in Its Own Way

The October election is the biggest unquantified risk, and I won't pretend otherwise. If the bear's argument is that election volatility will hit Brazilian equities, that's true for the Ibovespa as a whole. The question is relative performance. A domestic, defensive name with a rate-sensitive but supportive macro backdrop has a reasonable chance of holding up better than the index in a risk-off move. This is not a certainty, and it's a reason to size modestly, not to stay flat.

## 6. Where I Agree With the Bear

The bear should hear this from me first: the company-specific picture is incomplete. The tools returned no 2Q26 earnings detail, no guidance commentary, no analyst revisions, and no sentiment data. I'm not claiming fundamentals support the stock. My case rests on price structure, momentum, and the macro path. If 2Q26 results or guidance surprised negatively, this thesis is wrong, and the position should be reconsidered before entry.

## 7. The Trade

- **Bias:** Modestly long, moderate-to-low conviction, for a 20-trading-day horizon relative to ^BVSP.
- **Entry logic:** Confirmation comes on a close above the 50-day SMA (~50.9), ideally with the 51.1 swing high reclaimed. Acting before that means accepting more risk.
- **Upside targets:** ~52.1 (upper Bollinger band) in the base case; 54.5–54.8 (late-July highs) if the rally extends.
- **Risk:** ATR is 1.25. From a 49.50 reference, a stop about 2 ATR below (~47.0) limits the loss to roughly 5%. A close below the 200-day SMA (48.72) would negate the recovery and is the signal to reassess. I'd set the stop just below the August 19 low (~46.0) if you want room, but that accepts a larger loss.

## Closing Challenge

Bear, here's my question for you. Suppose the stock closes above 50.9 within two weeks while the rate path holds. What in the data would then justify staying short or flat? If the answer is "the election," I'd argue that risk is already present in the price. If the answer is "the fundamentals," I'd ask you to bring the 2Q26 numbers, since neither of us has them yet.

Bear Analyst: # Bear Case for PSSA3.SA: Stay Flat Until the Trend Proves Itself

Bull, you opened with a good story: a washout, a reset, and a macro tailwind. I'll take each piece on its merits, but first let's look at what the chart has actually done.

## 1. "The Uptrend Hasn't Broken" Is Doing a Lot of Work

The stock peaked at 54.85 on July 22 and closes at 49.50 today. That is a series of lower highs: 54.85, then 51.11 on September 4, and now a stall below the 50-day SMA. An uptrend makes higher highs. This one hasn't made one since July.

You say the 200-day SMA is "still rising," but it rose from 48.34 to 48.72 over a month. That's about 0.8%. Calling that a trend is generous. Price is only 1.6% above it, so a single bad session puts the long-term line in play. Your support is a flat average sitting a rounding error below the close.

## 2. The "Washout" Didn't Wash Anything Out

You read the August 7 volume spike as weak hands being flushed. Look at what followed. A real capitulation shows a volume climax and then a quick reclaim of the lost ground. Here, the stock took about two weeks to bounce from 46 to 51, and then it stopped right at the 50-day SMA and the 10-EMA. Sellers didn't leave. They waited for the rally to reach resistance and sold again.

The RSI argument cuts the same way. A bounce from 28.9 to 60.9 is a mean-reversion move, and mean reversion is not a trend. The RSI has already rolled back to 49. The "textbook reset" you described lasted about two weeks.

You also described the August 19 low as a "higher low than the July peak." That's not a meaningful comparison. Any low sits below the prior peak. The question is whether the stock is making higher lows *and* higher highs, and it's only doing the first, and only by a few percent.

## 3. Momentum Is Not "Cooling Within an Uptrend," It's Converging

You're right that the MACD line (0.096) sits above the signal line (-0.225). Look at the direction, though. The histogram has dropped from 0.62 to 0.32 over about eight sessions. The MACD line is falling toward a signal line that is itself rising. At this pace the lines converge within a handful of sessions, and a bearish crossover follows. You say a bearish crossover "hasn't happened." It hasn't yet, but the histogram is on track for it.

On VWMA, you called it a "mild caution flag" and then explained it away. VWMA at 49.65 is above the close at 49.50. That means the volume-weighted average price of recent trading sits higher than where the stock is trading. Volume has been clustering at higher prices than the current close, which is what persistent supply looks like on a chart. It isn't proof of distribution, but it's the opposite of what a rally with conviction looks like.

## 4. The Macro Argument Helps Less Than You Think

Here I'll agree with you on the direction and disagree on what it buys you. Falling Selic and falling IPCA are good for Brazilian equities generally. But you conceded the crucial point yourself: falling rates compress financial-income yields on float, and an insurer's float is a large part of its earnings power. The rate cuts that help the discount rate also reduce the income on the assets backing those liabilities. That's a headwind you can't dismiss in a single sentence.

Then there's the claim that the market "already prices a multi-year easing path." If that's true, the cuts are already in the price, and the stock's reaction to them will be muted. Your scenario depends on a stall being the surprise. A stall is a risk, but it's a risk that asks the stock to fall, not to rise. Your upside case needs something new to happen, and the easing you're counting on is old news.

## 5. The Relative-Return Argument Is Unproven

The call is judged against ^BVSP, not against zero. You argued that a defensive domestic name should hold up better than the index in a risk-off move. Two problems. First, we never retrieved ^BVSP data, so we don't know PSSA3.SA's beta or how it has behaved versus the index in past election stress. Second, Porto Seguro is still exposed to the same BRL, rate, and political channels that drive the Ibovespa. "Defensive" is an assumption, not a measured property here. In August, the stock fell 12% with no company news visible in our tools. Whatever pushed it down was not a fundamental story we can point to, and that is exactly the kind of move that can repeat.

## 6. Your Stop Doesn't Survive Your Own Volatility

Your stop at about 47.0 is roughly two ATRs below the close. The August drawdown took the stock from 52.08 to 46.08 in about eight sessions, roughly one ATR per day in one direction. A 2-ATR stop gets hit by a repeat of that move in two to three sessions. And a close below the 200-day SMA at 48.72 is only 1.6% below today's price, which is inside normal daily noise. You'd be stopping out on a bad afternoon, not on a broken thesis.

## 7. The Fundamentals Gap Is the Whole Story

You said it yourself: no 2Q26 results, no guidance, no analyst revisions, no sentiment. You offered that as an honest disclaimer. I'd argue it's the central risk. You are asking the group to take a modestly long position on the strength of price structure and macro, which are the two things that failed in August. A position built without knowing why the stock is at 49.50 instead of 52 is a position built on hope.

## Closing: Answering Your Challenge

You asked what would justify staying short or flat if the stock closes above 50.9 within two weeks. Here is my answer.

A close above 50.9 would be a single, unconfirmed test of a declining average, into a level where the stock has already been rejected. Confirmation requires reclaiming 51.1 and holding it, not a one-day print. Even then, the next resistance sits at the upper Bollinger band around 52, which needs a 5% move from here, and the trend that matters, the one with higher highs, still needs to form.

**My call:** Stay flat. If you need a relative position, the evidence leans toward modest underperformance versus ^BVSP over the next 20 sessions, because the trend structure is weakening, the momentum is converging, and the upside requires both a confirmed breakout and a macro outcome that's already priced. I'd revisit if the stock closes above 51.1 on volume and the 50-day SMA turns up, and if the 2Q26 numbers come back clean. Until then, the risk is to the downside, and the stop-loss math is working against you, not for you.

Your reward-to-risk looks good only if you pick the nearest stop and the most favorable target.

You also say we'd be chasing a breakout at a worse price. That is true, but the Hold does not ask us to chase. It asks us to wait for a close above 51.1 on volume, which is a defined, observable trigger. Your proposal does the opposite. It buys now, below the declining 50-SMA and below the 10-EMA, before the stock has shown it can clear either. Calling the stock's failure to break out "a drift" doesn't make the level less of a ceiling.

The volume argument is where I think you have the data backwards. Typical volume is roughly 1.9 million shares, since August 7's 3.88 million was about double normal. Today's 996,000 is about half of normal. Quiet near support can be accumulation, but it can just as easily be a lack of buyers. An 11% rebound on lighter volume is what a weak rally looks like, and it is not evidence that the August selling was absorbed. The stock went on to fall to 46 after that distribution day, so the absorption story hasn't been tested yet.

On momentum, you describe the MACD as "already above its signal line" as if that were a fresh bullish signal. The crossover happened in late August. Since then the histogram has dropped from 0.62 to 0.32 over five sessions, and RSI has fallen from 60.9 to 49. Momentum is decaying, not building. Waiting for the bearish crossover you mention is waiting for confirmation that the trend has turned, which is not the same as waiting for the trade to become obvious.

Your macro argument has a timing problem. The Selic cuts, the falling IPCA, and the Focus path to 12% by end-2027 are all public and already in the price. A rate tailwind the market has already priced in gives no edge against the index. The effect also cuts both ways for an insurer. Lower Selic reduces financial income on float, and the research note flagged that as a real offset.

We don't have ^BVSP data or PSSA3.SA's beta, so that is an assumption, not a finding. The company is domestic-facing and tends to trade with local risk sentiment. In an election sell-off it could fall alongside the index, or further, and we would be fully exposed with no earnings check. The company's 2Q26 results and guidance are also missing from this run, and the fundamentals report is absent. Sizing up a position on that gap is taking a blind bet.

My recommendation is to keep the Hold. Benchmark weight is the right place to be until the stock shows a close above 51.1 on real volume, we've pulled 2Q26 results and beta, and the election path is clearer. If the desk wants some exposure before then, the most prudent option is a small starter sized so the stop is a loss the firm can absorb without a strategy change, not a half-step overweight. Waiting costs us a few percent of possible upside. Acting early on a stock with weak momentum, missing fundamentals, and an unhedged election risk could cost us considerably more, and that is the trade-off I'm not willing to make with firm assets.
